crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: The AI Enablement Audit in Investment Firms
children.blurb: The AI enablement audit in investment firms examines how artificial intelligence is used across investment processes, from research and portfolio construction to trading, compliance, and client reporting.

children.name: Fair Lending and Bias Testing
children.blurb: Fair lending and bias testing examines whether credit, mortgage, and other lending models treat applicants differently on protected characteristics like race, sex, age, or national origin.

children.name: Explaining Models to Regulators and Clients
children.blurb: Explaining models to regulators and clients covers the practice of translating how a model works, what data it uses, and what its outputs mean into language that a non-specialist can act on.

children.name: Protecting Material Non-Public Information
children.blurb: Protecting material non-public information in AI-related firms covers the handling of confidential data about models, training runs, partnerships, regulatory findings, and financial results before public disclosure.

children.name: Verifying What a Model Produced
children.blurb: Verifying what a model produced covers the practices used to confirm that an AI system's outputs are accurate, consistent with their inputs, and fit for the purpose a firm assigns them.

sections.body: This field is about making sure AI systems inside financial institutions can be checked, explained, and kept within legal and ethical bounds. It covers audits of how a firm enables AI, tests for bias in lending decisions, explanations of model behavior for regulators and clients, protection of confidential data, and verification of what a model actually produced. In practice, investment firms now run structured reviews before deploying a model, checking data sources, access controls, and fallback procedures. Fair lending teams run statistical tests on credit models to see whether outcomes differ by protected class. Compliance officers produce plain language summaries of model logic for examiners. Data loss prevention tools monitor prompts and outputs for material non-public information. Verification work reconstructs the inputs and steps behind a specific output so a firm can show what happened.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven. Basic audit checklists and bias testing for traditional credit models are well established, but explaining large language models remains hard because their reasoning is not directly inspectable. Data loss prevention can catch obvious leaks of known confidential text, but it misses paraphrased or inferred information, and verification of model output is often possible only when the firm logs every prompt, retrieval step, and generation parameter. The honest limit is that no current method gives a complete guarantee that a model has not learned or repeated protected information, and regulators are still forming expectations. The site's 210 compliance and regulation pages reflect how much of this area is still being written.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader starting with The AI Enablement Audit in Investment Firms gets the front door view of how a firm decides what AI is safe to use and who is accountable. Fair Lending and Bias Testing narrows to the specific statistical checks required before a credit model can be used. Explaining Models to Regulators and Clients covers the communication problem, turning model internals into defensible summaries. Protecting Material Non-Public Information addresses the leak risk from prompts, training data, and outputs. Verifying What a Model Produced closes the loop by showing how to reconstruct and prove what a model did after the fact.
